explainer.summary: WETH9 is a simple wrapper contract that accepts ETH via deposit or fallback and mints equivalent WETH balances while allowing withdrawal back to ETH. It implements ERC20-style functions using balanceOf and allowance mappings with no access control or owner. totalSupply returns the contract's ETH balance and all operations are performed directly on msg.sender or approved addresses.

key_functions.name: deposit
key_functions.what: Accepts msg.value and increases balanceOf[msg.sender] by that amount while emitting Deposit.

key_functions.name: withdraw
key_functions.what: Requires sufficient balanceOf[msg.sender], reduces it by wad, transfers ETH via msg.sender.transfer(wad), and emits Withdrawal.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowance[msg.sender][guy] to wad and emits Approval.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Calls transferFrom(msg.sender, dst, wad) to move tokens.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Checks balanceOf[src] >= wad, deducts from allowance if needed (except for uint(-1)), updates balances, and emits Transfer.

key_functions.name: totalSupply
key_functions.what: Returns this.balance as the total supply.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; the contract contains no proxy, owner, or selfdestruct logic and is deployed as a standalone immutable contract.
user_risks: withdraw performs an external transfer after state update but callers must still handle potential reentrancy in custom logic.
transferFrom allows unlimited allowance via uint(-1) which never decreases on use.
integration_tips: Call deposit with ETH or send ETH directly to the contract to wrap.
Use withdraw to unwrap WETH back to ETH.
Integrate via standard ERC20 approve/transferFrom for spending WETH.

explainer.summary: TetherToken implements an ERC20 token with additional controls from Pausable, BlackList, and Ownable. It applies optional transfer fees, supports blacklisting with fund destruction, and includes a deprecation flag to forward calls to an upgraded contract. Owner-only functions allow issuing/redeeming tokens, pausing, and parameter changes.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Transfers tokens applying fee if set, checks not paused and not blacklisted, forwards to upgraded if deprecated.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Transfers from allowance applying fee, checks not paused and not blacklisted, forwards if deprecated.

key_functions.name: issue
key_functions.what: Increases totalSupply and owner balance by amount, only callable by owner.

key_functions.name: redeem
key_functions.what: Decreases totalSupply and owner balance by amount, only callable by owner.

key_functions.name: deprecate
key_functions.what: Sets deprecated true and upgradedAddress, only by owner.

key_functions.name: addBlackList
key_functions.what: Marks address as blacklisted, only by owner.

key_functions.name: destroyBlackFunds
key_functions.what: Zeros balance of blacklisted address and reduces totalSupply, only by owner.

key_functions.name: pause
key_functions.what: Sets paused true, only by owner when not paused.

key_functions.name: setParams
key_functions.what: Sets basisPointsRate and maximumFee with hardcoded limits, only by owner.

admin_powers: add and remove addresses from blacklist
explainer.upgradeability: When deprecated is true, transfer/transferFrom/approve/balanceOf/allowance/totalSupply forward to UpgradedStandardToken at upgradedAddress via transferByLegacy etc.; set only by owner via deprecate.
user_risks: transfers blocked when paused
blacklisted addresses cannot send tokens and may lose funds via destroyBlackFunds
transfer fees may be applied up to set limits
totalSupply can increase or decrease via owner issue/redeem
contract may be deprecated requiring interaction with new address
integration_tips: check paused state and isBlackListed before expecting transfers to succeed
account for possible fees reducing received amount in transfer/transferFrom
monitor Deprecate event and switch to upgradedAddress if set
use onlyPayloadSize protected calls for approve/transfer to avoid short address issues
totalSupply and balances may change via issue/redeem/destroyBlackFunds

explainer.summary: FiatTokenV2_2 extends FiatTokenV2_1 and adds initializeV2_2 to migrate deprecated blacklists and update the token symbol while setting _initializedVersion to 3. It overrides balance/blacklist storage in balanceAndBlacklistStates (high bit flags blacklist), _domainSeparator for EIP712 with version "2", and several ERC20/permit methods to enforce whenNotPaused and notBlacklisted checks. Signature-based authorization functions (permit, transferWithAuthorization, etc.) and approve/increase/decreaseAllowance are re-exposed with the same modifiers.

key_functions.name: initializeV2_2
key_functions.what: Requires _initializedVersion==2, sets symbol, migrates accountsToBlacklist from _deprecatedBlacklisted to _blacklist, blacklists contract itself, and sets _initializedVersion=3.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused wrapper calling _permit with bytes signature (or v,r,s overload).

key_functions.name: transferWithAuthorization
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused notBlacklisted wrapper calling _transferWithAuthorization.

key_functions.name: receiveWithAuthorization
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused notBlacklisted wrapper calling _receiveWithAuthorization with payee check.

key_functions.name: cancelAuthorization
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused wrapper calling _cancelAuthorization.

key_functions.name: _setBlacklistState
key_functions.what: Internal override that ORs (1<<255) into balanceAndBlacklistStates or resets to _balanceOf.

key_functions.name: _setBalance
key_functions.what: Internal override enforcing <=(2^255-1) and not blacklisted before writing balance.

key_functions.name: _isBlacklisted
key_functions.what: Internal view override returning (balanceAndBlacklistStates[_account]>>255)==1.

key_functions.name: _balanceOf
key_functions.what: Internal view override masking balanceAndBlacklistStates[_account] & ((1<<255)-1).

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: External override whenNotPaused calling _approve.

explainer.upgradeability: Uses _initializedVersion (checked==2 then set to 3) inside initializeV2_2; no proxy or upgrade logic present in this file.
user_risks: Blacklisted accounts cannot transfer or have balances updated.
Balances cannot exceed (2^255-1).
All state-changing calls revert when paused.
integration_tips: Call initializeV2_2 once with accountsToBlacklist and newSymbol after V2_1 initialization.
Use packed r,s,v signatures for permit and authorization methods.
Check _isBlacklisted and paused state before integrating transfers.

explainer.summary: Dai is an ERC20 token contract with authorization controls via wards, mint/burn capabilities restricted to authorized addresses, and EIP-712 permit support for approvals. It inherits LibNote for event logging via the note modifier on auth functions. The contract sets the deployer as the initial ward in the constructor and defines DOMAIN_SEPARATOR for permits.

key_functions.name: rely
key_functions.what: Adds an address to wards mapping, granting authorization (requires auth).

key_functions.name: deny
key_functions.what: Removes an address from wards mapping (requires auth).

key_functions.name: mint
key_functions.what: Increases balance and totalSupply for a user (requires auth).

key_functions.name: burn
key_functions.what: Decreases balance and totalSupply after allowance/balance checks.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens with allowance deduction unless infinite approval.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowance and emits Approval event.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Sets allowance via EIP-712 signature after nonce, expiry, and signature validation.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Calls transferFrom from msg.sender.

explainer.upgradeability: No upgradeability mechanism or proxy pattern is present in the contract.
user_risks: Wards can mint unlimited DAI.
Wards can be added/removed only by existing wards.
integration_tips: Permit supports infinite allowance via allowed=true setting wad to uint(-1).
Nonces must be tracked off-chain to avoid invalid-nonce reverts.
Use transferFrom for moves between arbitrary addresses.

explainer.summary: UniswapV2Factory (constructor takes _feeToSetter) deploys UniswapV2Pair instances via CREATE2 in createPair after enforcing tokenA != tokenB, token0 != address(0) and no existing pair. It exposes getPair/allPairs views, allPairsLength, and two admin-only setters that update feeTo/feeToSetter. The factory address is stored immutably in each pair at construction and used for feeTo lookups during mint/burn.

key_functions.name: createPair
key_functions.what: Validates distinct non-zero tokens, deploys UniswapV2Pair with CREATE2 using salt = keccak256(token0,token1), calls initialize, stores the pair in both directions of getPair and appends to allPairs, emits PairCreated.

key_functions.name: setFeeTo
key_functions.what: Requires msg.sender == feeToSetter then writes the supplied address to feeTo storage.

key_functions.name: setFeeToSetter
key_functions.what: Requires msg.sender == feeToSetter then writes the supplied address to feeToSetter storage.

key_functions.name: getPair
key_functions.what: Public mapping returning the pair address for any (token0,token1) combination.

key_functions.name: allPairs
key_functions.what: Public array returning the pair address at a given index; length exposed via allPairsLength.

key_functions.name: allPairsLength
key_functions.what: Returns the current length of the allPairs array.

admin_powers: feeToSetter may call setFeeTo to change the recipient of protocol fees
feeToSetter may call setFeeToSetter to transfer the admin role to any address
explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; no proxy, delegatecall or owner-controlled replacement logic present in the source.
user_risks: createPair can be called by anyone; duplicate or malicious token pairs are prevented only by the EXISTING_PAIR and IDENTICAL_ADDRESS checks
Protocol fees are sent to feeTo only when feeTo != address(0) and only on liquidity events after kLast is set
integration_tips: Call createPair with the two ERC20 addresses in either order; the lower address becomes token0
Use the getPair mapping or allPairs array to discover existing pairs instead of deploying duplicates
Pairs store factory immutably; feeTo is read from the factory on every mint/burn that may trigger _mintFee

explainer.summary: UniswapV2Router02 is the canonical entrypoint contract for Uniswap V2 liquidity and swaps, deployed with immutable factory and WETH addresses in its constructor. It implements IUniswapV2Router02 by routing calls to pairs via UniswapV2Library helpers, enforcing deadlines via the ensure modifier, and handling both standard and fee-on-transfer token flows. The contract contains no owner or privileged functions and is not upgradeable.

key_functions.name: addLiquidity
key_functions.what: Creates pair if needed, calculates optimal amounts, transfers tokens to pair and mints liquidity.

key_functions.name: addLiquidityETH
key_functions.what: Wraps ETH to WETH, adds liquidity with a token, refunds excess ETH.

key_functions.name: removeLiquidity
key_functions.what: Transfers LP tokens to pair, burns them and returns underlying tokens after minimum checks.

key_functions.name: removeLiquidityETH
key_functions.what: Removes liquidity for token+WETH, unwraps WETH and sends ETH to recipient.

key_functions.name: swapExactTokensForTokens
key_functions.what: Transfers input, calls _swap to route through path, enforces amountOutMin.

key_functions.name: swapExactETHForTokens
key_functions.what: Wraps msg.value, performs ETH->token swap via path, refunds dust.

key_functions.name: _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens
key_functions.what: Internal loop that reads post-transfer balances to compute output for fee-on-transfer tokens.

key_functions.name: swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens
key_functions.what: Transfers input then uses balance delta check instead of precomputed amounts.

key_functions.name: quote
key_functions.what: Pure wrapper to UniswapV2Library.quote for price calculation.

key_functions.name: getAmountsOut
key_functions.what: View wrapper to UniswapV2Library.getAmountsOut using current reserves.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; factory and WETH are immutable, constructor only sets them once.
user_risks: Deadline must be >= block.timestamp or transaction reverts with EXPIRED.
amountOutMin / amountAMin checks can still fail due to front-running or price movement.
Fee-on-transfer tokens require the Supporting variants; standard swaps may under-deliver.
Path must start with WETH for ETH swaps and end with WETH for ETH outputs.
integration_tips: Always pass a deadline slightly in the future and re-estimate amounts just before sending tx.
Use getAmountsOut / getAmountsIn to compute min amounts and validate path length.
For fee-on-transfer tokens call the SupportingFeeOnTransferTokens variants and check balance delta.
Approve the router only for the exact amount needed or use permit variants to avoid allowance griefing.

explainer.summary: SwapRouter is a stateless contract for executing exact-input and exact-output swaps on Uniswap V3 pools, supporting single-hop and multi-hop paths via encoded bytes. It inherits PeripheryImmutableState (factory + WETH9 set at construction), PeripheryValidation (deadline checks), PeripheryPaymentsWithFee, Multicall, and SelfPermit; all swap logic lives in exactInputInternal/exactOutputInternal and the uniswapV3SwapCallback. No admin functions or upgrade mechanisms are present in the source.

key_functions.name: exactInputSingle
key_functions.what: Performs a single-hop exact-input swap with amountOutMinimum and sqrtPriceLimitX96 checks.

key_functions.name: exactInput
key_functions.what: Loops over a multi-hop path, calling exactInputInternal for each pool and enforcing amountOutMinimum at the end.

key_functions.name: exactOutputSingle
key_functions.what: Performs a single-hop exact-output swap, resetting amountInCached after the call.

key_functions.name: exactOutput
key_functions.what: Initiates an exact-output multi-hop swap via exactOutputInternal and reads the final amountIn from amountInCached.

key_functions.name: uniswapV3SwapCallback
key_functions.what: Validates the pool callback, decodes SwapCallbackData, pays the required tokenIn, and handles chained exact-output hops.

key_functions.name: multicall
key_functions.what: Executes an array of delegatecalls to this contract and returns the results or reverts with the inner string.

key_functions.name: selfPermit
key_functions.what: Calls IERC20Permit.permit on a token to approve this router for a given value and deadline.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; constructor sets immutable factory and WETH9, and no proxy or owner logic exists in the source.
user_risks: Transactions revert if block.timestamp exceeds the supplied deadline.
Swaps can fail the amountOutMinimum or amountInMaximum check, returning no tokens.
Multi-hop paths require the caller to have approved the first token; intermediate custody is held by the router.
amountInCached is transient and must be reset after exactOutputSingle/exactOutput to avoid stale reads.
integration_tips: Batch approvals and swaps in one transaction by embedding selfPermit* calls inside multicall.
Set sqrtPriceLimitX96 to 0 for no price limit; otherwise the pool may not deliver the full amountOut.
Use address(0) as recipient to have the router custody intermediate tokens for multi-hop exactInput.
Wrap ETH via the receive() handler only when paying with WETH9 in PeripheryPayments.pay.

explainer.summary: Permit2 (src/Permit2.sol) is a non-upgradeable contract that inherits SignatureTransfer and AllowanceTransfer to provide a unified interface for EIP-712 signature-based token transfers and stored-allowance transfers. It relies on EIP712 for domain separation with chain-id caching, uses PackedAllowance storage for per-owner/token/spender approvals, and enforces nonce and deadline checks via libraries such as PermitHash and SignatureVerification. All transfer functions require prior ERC-20 approval to the Permit2 contract itself.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Updates amount and expiration for a token/spender in the allowance mapping and emits Approval.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Verifies an EIP-712 PermitSingle or PermitBatch signature, then calls _updateApproval to store the new allowance values.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens using a stored PackedAllowance, checking expiration and decrementing the amount unless it is type(uint160).max.

key_functions.name: lockdown
key_functions.what: Zeroes the amount field for each TokenSpenderPair supplied by msg.sender and emits Lockdown.

key_functions.name: invalidateNonces
key_functions.what: Sets a strictly higher nonce on a PackedAllowance, limited to a uint16 delta, and emits NonceInvalidation.

key_functions.name: permitTransferFrom
key_functions.what: Validates a PermitTransferFrom or PermitBatchTransferFrom signature, marks the unordered nonce, and executes the requested safeTransferFrom calls.

key_functions.name: permitWitnessTransferFrom
key_functions.what: Same as permitTransferFrom but includes an additional witness hash for custom typed data.

key_functions.name: invalidateUnorderedNonces
key_functions.what: ORs a mask into nonceBitmap[msg.sender][wordPos] and emits UnorderedNonceInvalidation.

key_functions.name: DOMAIN_SEPARATOR
key_functions.what: Returns the cached EIP-712 domain separator or rebuilds it if block.chainid has changed since deployment.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; the contract contains only immutable state and no proxy or owner-controlled upgrade logic.
user_risks: Signatures become permanently invalid after their sigDeadline or deadline timestamp.
Re-using a nonce (ordered or unordered) reverts with InvalidNonce.
Allowances automatically expire after the stored expiration value; transfers attempted afterward revert.
Lockdown and nonce invalidation are irreversible and affect all future permits for the caller.
integration_tips: Call ERC-20 approve(Permit2, amount) before any transferFrom or permit that relies on stored allowances.
Use permit or permitTransferFrom with EIP-712 signatures to avoid separate approve transactions.
Batch variants accept arrays but still require matching lengths and valid nonces for every item.
Witness variants allow attaching extra data; the witnessTypeString must exactly match the appended EIP-712 type string.

explainer.summary: The Uni contract implements an ERC20 token (name=Uniswap, symbol=UNI, decimals=18, initial totalSupply=1_000_000_000e18) with a single minter address that can mint up to 2% of supply once per year after mintingAllowedAfter. It adds EIP-2612 permit, vote delegation with checkpoints, and uses SafeMath plus 96-bit safe casts throughout. All logic is contained in the single Uni.sol file with no proxy or upgrade mechanisms.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Sets initial balances[account] to totalSupply, records minter and mintingAllowedAfter.

key_functions.name: setMinter
key_functions.what: Allows current minter to replace the minter address.

key_functions.name: mint
key_functions.what: Minter-only function that increases totalSupply and dst balance by up to mintCap percent after the time lock.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Sets allowance via EIP-712 signature using PERMIT_TYPEHASH and DOMAIN_TYPEHASH.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Moves tokens and calls _moveDelegates.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens after checking allowance, then calls _moveDelegates.

key_functions.name: delegate
key_functions.what: Records new delegate and moves existing balance votes.

key_functions.name: delegateBySig
key_functions.what: Delegates via EIP-712 signature using DELEGATION_TYPEHASH.

key_functions.name: getPriorVotes
key_functions.what: Binary-searches checkpoints to return votes at a past blockNumber.

admin_powers: minter can call setMinter to change the minter address
minter can call mint to create up to 2% of totalSupply once per year
explainer.upgradeability: None; the contract contains no proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade logic.
user_risks: totalSupply can increase via mint
96-bit arithmetic reverts on values >= 2^96
delegation changes affect getPriorVotes results used by governance
integration_tips: Use allowance/transferFrom or permit for approvals; infinite approval supported via uint(-1)
Call getPriorVotes with finalized block numbers only
Track DelegateChanged and DelegateVotesChanged events for vote tracking

explainer.summary: LinkToken is a fixed-supply ERC20 token (totalSupply=10**27) that inherits StandardToken and ERC677Token, minting the entire supply to the deployer in the constructor. All transfers, transferFrom, approve and transferAndCall are guarded by the validRecipient modifier that rejects address(0) and the token contract itself. The contract contains no owner, no mint/burn, and no upgrade logic.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: moves tokens after checking validRecipient

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: moves tokens using allowance after checking validRecipient

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: sets allowance after checking validRecipient

key_functions.name: transferAndCall
key_functions.what: calls super.transfer then invokes onTokenTransfer on contract recipients

key_functions.name: balanceOf
key_functions.what: returns balances mapping value

key_functions.name: allowance
key_functions.what: returns allowed mapping value

key_functions.name: increaseApproval
key_functions.what: adds to allowance and emits Approval

key_functions.name: decreaseApproval
key_functions.what: subtracts from allowance (or sets to zero) and emits Approval

explainer.upgradeability: none present; contract is not behind a proxy and contains no upgrade or ownership mechanisms
user_risks: approve race condition mitigated only by increase/decreaseApproval helpers
transferAndCall silently succeeds even if recipient contract reverts in onTokenTransfer
integration_tips: use transferAndCall when interacting with Chainlink or other ERC677 receivers
check allowance before transferFrom because decreaseApproval can zero the value
recipient addresses must not be zero or the token contract itself

explainer.summary: GnosisSafe v1.3.0 is the singleton master copy (constructor sets threshold=1 to prevent direct use) that proxies delegate to; it implements multisig execution via EIP-712 SafeTx hashes, owner/threshold management (via inherited OwnerManager), module setup, optional guards, and fallback handlers. Core logic lives in setup (initializes owners, threshold, fallbackHandler, modules and optional payment), execTransaction (increments nonce, checks signatures via checkNSignatures, executes via Executor, handles payment), and supporting functions like checkSignatures, approveHash, encodeTransactionData and getTransactionHash.

key_functions.name: setup
key_functions.what: Initializes owners/threshold (via setupOwners), fallbackHandler (internalSetFallbackHandler), modules (setupModules) and optional payment; emits SafeSetup; can only be called once.

key_functions.name: execTransaction
key_functions.what: Encodes tx data, increments nonce, verifies required signatures with checkSignatures, optionally runs Guard checks, executes via execute, pays refund via handlePayment and emits success/failure events.

key_functions.name: checkNSignatures
key_functions.what: Validates exactly requiredSignatures from the packed signatures array supporting ECDSA (v=27/28 or eth_sign v>30), approved hashes (v=1) and contract signatures (v=0) using ISignatureValidator.isValidSignature.

key_functions.name: handlePayment
key_functions.what: Calculates and transfers gasUsed+baseGas payment in ETH or ERC20 token to refundReceiver (or tx.origin); reverts on transfer failure.

key_functions.name: approveHash
key_functions.what: Marks a hash as approved by a current owner in approvedHashes mapping; only callable by owners.

key_functions.name: encodeTransactionData
key_functions.what: Returns the EIP-712 prefixed bytes (0x1901 + domainSeparator + SAFE_TX_TYPEHASH struct) used for signing and txHash computation.

key_functions.name: setGuard
key_functions.what: Authorized function that stores a Guard address in GUARD_STORAGE_SLOT; the guard's checkTransaction/checkAfterExecution are invoked around execTransaction.

key_functions.name: setFallbackHandler
key_functions.what: Authorized function that stores handler in FALLBACK_HANDLER_STORAGE_SLOT; fallback delegates non-value calls to it.

admin_powers: Owners (via execTransaction or direct calls where authorized) can change owners/threshold, add/remove modules, set guard or fallbackHandler, and approve hashes.
Guard contract (if set) can inspect every transaction before/after execution.
Fallback handler (if set) receives all otherwise unhandled calls.
explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; this contract is the immutable singleton master copy referenced by GnosisSafeProxy instances (singleton storage slot must be first).
user_risks: Incorrect signature threshold or owner set during setup permanently locks the Safe.
Guard or fallbackHandler can arbitrarily inspect or redirect calls if set via Safe transaction.
Payment logic always transfers fees even on failed inner execution when gasPrice > 0.
integration_tips: Use getTransactionHash/encodeTransactionData to produce the exact bytes owners must sign.
Call execTransaction with packed signatures (r,s,v) in the order of increasing owner addresses.
For estimation only, requiredTxGas executes and reverts with the gas figure (deprecated).
Modules and guards must be added only through Safe transactions (SelfAuthorized checks).

explainer.summary: Multicall3 aggregates multiple external calls into single transactions, providing backwards compatibility with Multicall and Multicall2 via structs Call, Call3, and Call3Value. It implements aggregate, tryAggregate, aggregate3, aggregate3Value, and block-related variants that execute target.call or target.call{value:} while enforcing success requirements via require or inline assembly reverts. Additional view functions return block.number, blockhash, balances, and chain metadata directly from EVM opcodes.

key_functions.name: aggregate
key_functions.what: Executes Call[] with require(success) on each target.call, returns blockNumber and returnData[]

key_functions.name: tryAggregate
key_functions.what: Executes Call[] optionally requiring success, returns Result[] with per-call success and returnData

key_functions.name: tryBlockAndAggregate
key_functions.what: Calls tryAggregate then returns blockNumber, blockHash, and Result[]

key_functions.name: blockAndAggregate
key_functions.what: Wrapper calling tryBlockAndAggregate(true, calls)

key_functions.name: aggregate3
key_functions.what: Executes Call3[] using allowFailure flag and assembly revert on failure when disallowed

key_functions.name: aggregate3Value
key_functions.what: Executes Call3Value[] forwarding per-call value, accumulates valAccumulator and requires msg.value == sum

key_functions.name: getEthBalance
key_functions.what: Returns addr.balance

key_functions.name: getBlockNumber
key_functions.what: Returns block.number

key_functions.name: getChainId
key_functions.what: Returns block.chainid

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; deployed as a static non-proxy contract with no owner, delegatecall, or storage modification logic.
user_risks: aggregate and blockAndAggregate revert entire transaction on any call failure
aggregate3Value reverts if msg.value != sum of call values
External calls use raw target.call allowing arbitrary state changes on targets
integration_tips: Use payable aggregate methods to save 24 gas per call as noted in contract comments
Prefer Call3/Call3Value with allowFailure=true for partial execution
Call getBlockHash, getBasefee, or getLastBlockHash for on-chain context without extra contracts

explainer.summary: ENSRegistryWithFallback extends ENSRegistry and stores an immutable reference to a prior ENS instance in the 'old' public variable, set once in the constructor. For any node where recordExists returns false it delegates owner/resolver/ttl reads to the old contract; all writes go through the new registry's authorised modifier and _setOwner logic. The root node (0x0) owner is set to the deploying address by the ENSRegistry constructor.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Accepts ENS _old, calls ENSRegistry constructor (setting root owner to msg.sender) and stores _old.

key_functions.name: resolver
key_functions.what: Returns old.resolver(node) when !recordExists(node), otherwise super.resolver(node).

key_functions.name: owner
key_functions.what: Returns old.owner(node) when !recordExists(node), otherwise super.owner(node) (which maps address(this) to 0x0).

key_functions.name: ttl
key_functions.what: Returns old.ttl(node) when !recordExists(node), otherwise super.ttl(node).

key_functions.name: setOwner
key_functions.what: Authorised modifier check then _setOwner + Transfer event (inherited).

key_functions.name: setSubnodeOwner
key_functions.what: Authorised check, computes keccak256(node,label), calls _setOwner, emits NewOwner (inherited).

key_functions.name: _setOwner
key_functions.what: Internal: if owner==0x0 stores address(this) instead, then writes to records[node].owner.

key_functions.name: setApprovalForAll
key_functions.what: Sets operators[msg.sender][operator] and emits ApprovalForAll (inherited).

admin_powers: Initial owner of node 0x0 (set in ENSRegistry constructor)
explainer.upgradeability: Fallback reads to immutable 'old' ENS instance for unmigrated nodes; no proxy or owner-controlled upgrade mechanism present.
user_risks: Root-node owner can call any authorised function on any node
Zero-address owners are stored as address(this) and appear as 0x0 externally
Operators approved via setApprovalForAll can modify any of an owner's nodes
integration_tips: Call recordExists before relying on owner/resolver/ttl to know whether data came from old or new registry
Use the public 'old' variable to query the legacy contract directly if needed
Authorised checks rely on both direct ownership and the operators mapping

explainer.summary: Seaport 1.5 (contracts/Seaport.sol) is a thin wrapper inheriting from Consideration that sets the contract name to Seaport via assembly in _name and _nameString. The constructor accepts a conduitController address and forwards it to the parent. No other logic is defined in the provided Seaport source.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Accepts conduitController address and passes it to Consideration constructor.

key_functions.name: _name
key_functions.what: Internal pure function returning Seaport name via assembly mstore and return.

key_functions.name: _nameString
key_functions.what: Internal pure function returning string 'Seaport'.

key_functions.name: _transfer

explainer.summary: Lido is the core liquid staking contract (v2) inheriting Versioned, StETHPermit and AragonApp; it accepts ETH via submit/fallback, mints stETH shares, buffers deposits, and processes oracle reports via handleOracleReport to update CL/EL balances, finalize withdrawals and mint fees. explainer.summary: The Pool contract serves as the primary entry point for Aave V3 market interactions, exposing supply, withdraw, borrow, repay, flashLoan, liquidationCall and related functions that delegate execution to libraries such as SupplyLogic, BorrowLogic and FlashLoanLogic. explainer.summary: CryptoPunksMarket is a Solidity 0.4.8 contract managing 10000 punks via punkIndexToAddress and balanceOf mappings, with Offer and Bid structs for sales and auctions. The single owner performs initial assignment via setInitialOwner/setInitialOwners before calling allInitialOwnersAssigned; thereafter users call getPunk, transferPunk, offerPunkForSale, buyPunk, enterBidForPunk and related functions. All state changes emit the corresponding events and pendingWithdrawals are used for payouts.

key_functions.what: Constructor sets owner, totalSupply=10000 and punksRemainingToAssign.

key_functions.name: setInitialOwner
key_functions.what: Owner-only function that assigns a punkIndex to an address before allPunksAssigned.

key_functions.name: setInitialOwners
key_functions.what: Owner-only batch wrapper that calls setInitialOwner for arrays of addresses and indices.

key_functions.name: allInitialOwnersAssigned
key_functions.what: Owner-only function that sets allPunksAssigned=true, enabling public minting and trading.

key_functions.name: getPunk
key_functions.what: Claims an unassigned punk when allPunksAssigned and punksRemainingToAssign > 0.

key_functions.name: transferPunk
key_functions.what: Transfers ownership of a punk the caller owns, cancelling any active offer and refunding a matching bid.

key_functions.name: offerPunkForSale
key_functions.what: Lists the caller's punk for sale at a minimum price to anyone.

key_functions.name: buyPunk
key_functions.what: Purchases an offered punk if msg.value meets the minValue and onlySellTo constraints.

key_functions.name: enterBidForPunk
key_functions.what: Submits a bid higher than any existing bid; previous bid is moved to pendingWithdrawals.

key_functions.name: acceptBidForPunk
key_functions.what: Seller accepts the current bid if it meets minPrice, transferring ownership and funds.

key_functions.name: withdraw
key_functions.what: Sends the caller's pendingWithdrawals balance after zeroing the mapping entry.

user_risks: All functions after initial assignment require allPunksAssigned=true or they throw.
Bids and offers are stored in public mappings; callers must verify punkIndexToAddress before acting.
withdraw uses the checks-effects-interactions pattern but any external call failure leaves funds in pendingWithdrawals.
integration_tips: Always call withdraw after buyPunk, acceptBidForPunk or a higher bid to retrieve ETH.
Read punksOfferedForSale and punkBids before calling buyPunk or acceptBidForPunk.
Use onlySellTo when calling offerPunkForSaleToAddress to restrict buyers.
